_comment: How old each section's DATA is allowed to get. Read by scripts/check-freshness.mjs, which runs in postbuild and npm test. `lastReviewed` is DECLARED, never detected: file mtime and git log both get reset by a formatting pass that changed no content, which is exactly how forty-day-old content read as current (LEDGER L-049). Move a date with `node scripts/check-freshness.mjs --touch <section>` when you have actually refreshed that content. Forgetting reports STALE, which errs safe. Seeded 2026-08-24 from the last real content change of each source, deliberately ignoring same-day commits that only changed colour tokens.
_states: fresh = inside budget. stale = past budget. rotten = past 2x budget. unknown = no date at all, which is a broken ledger and always fails. Whether ROTTEN fails the build is decided by breachMeans, not by the state alone.

repos.refresh: auto — GitHub API, every morning, early ET
repos.note: auto-refreshed; if this goes stale the refresh workflow has stopped doing its job

jobs.note: RESUMED 2026-09-26 (D76) after the D65 pause, retargeted (D75). FLIPPED to 'pipeline' on 2026-09-28, the condition D76 set: scheduled run 36453596258 scored every batch (1 of 1, 0 failed, none left out, none withheld). As 'pipeline' it is judged on lastReviewed, which refresh-data.yml's --touch jobs --if-changed stamps only on a run that WROTE a board: since 2026-10-06 the stamp skips when fetch-jobs.mjs kept the prior board. Before that it stamped every run, so the board sat kept from 09-29 to 10-06 while this date moved every morning and nothing alerted. Eight days with no board written now fails the build, podcast deploys included; an exhausted scoring key, every source down, or nothing clearing the floors is what that failure means. maxAgeDays stays 8: a morning that writes an identical board still moves lastReviewed, so a quiet week is not a fault.

Until then the source was Hermes’ model.public.json, frozen since 2026-09-15 with Hermes shut down on 2026-08-02. A job with no description is counted, not named, and the 5am window asks for one.

stack-counts.note: The doctrine version and the hook, skill and subagent counts on /stack/. CI cannot read this machine, so check-stack.mjs skips there and a stale snapshot deploys silently: it showed v45.1 against a real v48.2 for 12 days until 2026-09-24. The operator chose, 2026-09-24, a warning once the numbers pass seven days since the last export. Age counts from the last EXPORT, not the last change, because a run that found nothing new still proves the numbers current.

_budgets: Set by what the content DESCRIBES. 30d for anything describing a live system (builds, architectures, cron, apps, routines) because that is what goes wrong fastest. 45d for positioning and doctrine, which move slowly on purpose. 90d for the large reference sets, which genuinely do age slowly. Tight budgets on the auto-refreshed sections, where a breach means the PIPELINE stopped, not the content.
_breachMeans: What an overrun MEANS here, and it is declared per section because it cannot be derived. 'pipeline' = something automated moves this date, so an overrun means that machinery stopped — it FAILS the build, because a dead fetch should be loud. 'person' = a human moves this date, so an overrun means writing is overdue — it WARNS, because being behind on prose is no reason to hold a podcast episode or a deploy. PODCAST IS 'person' DESPITE BEING AUTOMATED: its date derives from the newest episode filename, so a gap means the producer stopped cutting releases, not that the sync broke (D30). Deriving this field from the `refresh` string would get that one case exactly wrong.
